title: Exporting clean project can result in "ERROR: _create_mesh_array must return at least a vertex array." messages
body: ### Tested versions - Reproduceable in: v4.5.stable.mono.official [876b29033] ### System information Godot v4.5.stable.mono - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7680) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-13900K (32 threads) - 127.7 GiB memory ### Issue description My team builds a product with many components, orchestrated through CMake. One component is a Godot project which we have CMake build by running --export-release, specifically something like this: > godot.windows.editor.dev.x86_64.mono.exe --headless --path [...] --verbose --export-release "Windows X64" [Destination executable path] Because Godot's exit code is always 0 even when there are export issues, I've been forced to write a wrapper tool which fails the build if there is any output to stderr (with a small exclusion list for known non-critical issues). One thing I am seeing now is the following error: > ERROR: _create_mesh_array must return at least a vertex array. at: (scene/resources/3d/primitive_meshes.cpp:56) I've traced this to the fact that one of our scenes has a MeshInstance3D node which uses a custom Mesh type that we wrote in C#, e.g. ```C# [Tool] [GlobalClass] public partial class InteractableShapeMesh : PrimitiveMesh ... ``` I debugged into the editor while exporting and the stack looks like this when the "_create_mesh_array must return at least a vertex array" message happens: ``` > Line 74 C kernel32.dll!BaseThreadInitThunk(unsigned long RunProcessInit, long(*)(void *) StartAddress, void * Argument) Line 77 C ntdll.dll!RtlUserThreadStart(long(*)(void *) StartAddress, void * Argument) Line 1184 C ``` And I can see the following code path gets hit giving a warning that a placeholder is being invoked: ```C++ Variant PlaceHolderScriptInstance::callp(const StringName &p_method, const Variant **p_args, int p_argcount, Callable::CallError &r_error) { r_error.error = Callable::CallError::CALL_ERROR_INVALID_METHOD; #if TOOLS_ENABLED if (Engine::get_singleton()->is_editor_hint()) { return String("Attempt to call a method on a placeholder instance. Check if the script is in tool mode."); ... ``` If I run --export-release back-to-back, the error messages are only on the first run. If I delete the .godot cache folder, the errors happen again. I also see the export error message in the Editor until I build, which is understandable. However, when running --export-release I would expect it to do things in an order that results in the newly built .NET assembly to be used and not need a "placeholder instance" since it doesn't have this error if the assembly already exists. My workaround for this is that I will be running "dotnet build" before invoking godot --export-release. This adds a little extra overhead (~1 second because the --export-release will run dotnet build incremental build again and find nothing changed), but it gives two nice benefits: 1. We see the C# compiler warnings and errors which are not shown when running --export-release 2. The "_create_mesh_array must return at least a vertex array." error no longer spews, presumably because a placeholder isn't used when the .NET assembly already exists. I am trying to integrate a Godot project into a bigger system and do it in a reliable way where CI gates can catch issues. My "fail on stderr" policy also ensures we keep things clean and avoid a lot of noisy errors, even if they are harmless. It seems like godot --export-release should be able to use the assembly that it just built and avoid this error message. The assembly is built before this error message is shown so it is at least done in the correct order. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a custom Mesh in C# and [Tool] attribute. Build it. 2. Create a scene with a MeshInstance3D and select the custom Mesh 3. Close Godot. Delete .godot folder 4. Run godot --export-release and observe "_create_mesh_array must return at least a vertex array." error message ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [dot-net-placeholder-export-repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22753146/dot-net-placeholder-export-repro.zip) And then repro like so (make sure .godot folder doesn't already exist) > Godot_v4.5-stable_mono_win64_console.exe --headless --export-release "Windows X64" Repro.exe Should see something like this: But run the export again and the errors are now gone.
